text.p: Heatwave conditions may result in problems in the Eastern USA through midweek. High temperatures will be in the 90sF along most of the East Coast. A back-door cold front may provide temporary relief in the New England coastal areas on Tuesday as winds come in from the cooler ocean. High temperatures of 95-100F are expected in Washington DC. Heat-related problems are likely, especially in that region.

The tropics are active in the eastern Pacific and Atlantic, but the threats are mostly to shipping at this time. Hurricane Enrique is about 1050 miles southwest of Baja in the eastern Pacific, and moving northwest. Top winds have peaked at 105 mph and are expected to begin to weaken. An organizing tropical disturbance about 700 miles south southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico, is expected to develop into a tropical depression by Monday night, with the threat to shipping increasing slowly. Tropical Storm Claudette has top winds of 45 mph and is in the Atlantic about 195 miles east southeast of Cape Hatteras, NC, moving north at 6 mph. This storm should turn northeast.
There are no further statements at this time.
